name: Perdatus (CR 1+)
body:
Perdatus is a template which can be applied to any non-mythic creature with an Intelligence score. It uses the abilities as the base creature, with the following modifications.

Challenge Rating: As base creature +1, +1 for every 2 mythic ranks the creature gains.

Alignment: A perdatus’ alignment shifts to chaotic evil.

Mythic Tier: A perdatus gains a number of mythic tiers equal to half its CR. It gains all of the cumulative abilities of its tier as specified on Table: Base Mythic Abilities but does not choose a mythic path.

Type: A perdatus gains the mythic subtype.

Defensive Abilities: A perdatus gains the following defensive ability.

Immortality (Ex)

When a perdatus is slain, its consciousness materializes somewhere else on the same planet in a new body of its creation. Most often, this body is very different from the original body, and GMs should create a new creature with the perdatus template to reflect the altered nature of this foe.

Special Attacks: A perdatus gains the following special attacks.

Inflammatory Presence (Su)

A perdatus exudes an aura which distorts the tensions of ideology. Creatures within 30 feet per mythic rank who can see and hear the perdatus must attempt a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 the perdatus’ Hit Dice + the perdatus’ Charisma modifier). Failing a Will save against a perdatus’ inflammatroy presence exacerbates the most destructive and volatile assumptions of the target’s belief system to the greatest extreme possible.

The target believes that all atrocities and processes of self-destruction are permissible or possibly even necessary for achieving their ideological goals, although this radicalization always results in the creature seeing the perdatus as an ally in these goals. This is a mind-affecting effect which lasts as long as the creature remains within range and for 24 hours thereafter. During this time, the perdatus typically seeks to reconnect with the creature and establish a perdition link with them. A perdatus can suppress or reactivate its inflammatory presence as a free action.

Special Qualities: A perdatus gains the following special qualities:

Accelerant Visions (Ex)

Attempts to interact directly with a perdatus’ thoughts (such as via detect thoughts or telepathy) expose the target to the perdatus’ unspeakable presence. If the perdatus is capable of making mental contact with creatures, it may attempt to use this ability through any means of telepathic communication they can use.

Perdition Link (Su)

A perdatus can form telepathic connections (known as perdition links) between itself and other creatures. A perdatus may add a willing creature within 30 feet per mythic rank to its perdition link in a process that takes 1 minute. If multiple perdati are created by the same culture, they are considered to always have each other in their perdition links. A perdatus may remove any number of creatures from their perdition link as an immediate action.

Any creature affected by the perdition link is continually affected as if it had failed its saving throw against inflammatory presence. A perdatus can communicate telepathically with any creature it has formed a perdition link with, this telepathy operating even across planes. All creatures within the link are considered valid targets for any spells, magic sphere effects, or psionic powers employed by the perdatus, and the perdatus may ignore any spell resistance, power resistance, or immunities possessed by creatures affected by the perdition link.

The perdition link can only be removed through psychic chirurgery, wish, miracle, or similarly powerful abilities, although a creature will actively attempt to resist having this condition removed. Identifying whether a creature is affected by perdition link requires a successful Sense Motive check (DC 25 + the perdatus’ CR).

Whenever the perdatus communicates telepathically with a creature through its perdition link, it may force the creature to attempt a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 the perdatus’ Hit Dice + the perdatus’ Charisma modifier). On a failed save, the creature is unaware that the perdatus attempted to communicate with it and assumes that any information or suggestions were either prior knowledge or something the creature devised itself.

Seamless Guise (Su)

A perdatus is immediately aware of all divination and clairsentience effects which would involve, expose, or target them, and may falsify the results of such effects in order to make it convey whatever information the perdatus desires. For example, a perdatus could cause itself to read as a weak good-aligned creature to a detect good spell, cause a scrying spell targeting it to show that it is in a different location, or remove any indication of its presence in an area affected by a prying eyes spell. Use of this ability in ways that directly conflict with demonstrable reality is most often the only way to find out that someone is a perdatus.

Ability Score Modifiers: +4 Intelligence, +4 Wisdom, +6 Charisma. These improvements are in addition to the ability score increases the perdatus may gain from mythic ranks.

Sample Perdatus

In the days before the Qlippoth War, Halken travelers would whisper of the sage who dwelt on the night roads. This “Wandering Prophet” always seemed to hold whatever secret the traveler desired and would tell them whatever they wished to hear, but this information would often stoke up grudges or incite frenzied acts of violence. Long after Halkenir’s fall, it is said that the Wandering Prophet still travels the Great Road, his incendiary whispers echoing through dreams and visions to touch the minds of survivors across the fallen empire.

Numerous cults across the Ashfields have established themselves as followers of the prophet, accelerating Halkenir’s ideals of hegemonic community into sectarian warmongering against other enclaves.
